title: Build Smart Campus Automation System with IoT monitoring and AI optimization

requirements.text: Create a backend data model for campus IoT devices including device ID, type (sensor/actuator), location (building, room), status (online/offline), and last reading timestamp
acceptanceCriteria: Device records can be created, read, updated, and deleted
Device status can be queried by location or type
Timestamp tracks last communication from each device

requirements.text: Implement backend functions to record and retrieve sensor readings (temperature, humidity, occupancy, energy consumption) with device ID, value, unit, and timestamp
acceptanceCriteria: Sensor readings are stored with device reference and timestamp
Historical readings can be queried by device and time range
Support for multiple sensor types with different units

requirements.text: Create backend automation rules system where rules define conditions (sensor thresholds) and actions (actuator commands) with enable/disable status
acceptanceCriteria: Rules can be created with condition logic and target actions
Rules can be enabled or disabled
Rules include metadata like name, description, and creation date

requirements.text: Implement backend optimization engine that analyzes sensor data patterns and generates recommendations for energy savings, space utilization, and operational efficiency
acceptanceCriteria: System analyzes historical sensor data to identify patterns
Recommendations are generated with priority levels
Each recommendation includes estimated impact and suggested actions

requirements.text: Build backend alert system that triggers notifications when sensor values exceed thresholds or devices go offline, with severity levels and acknowledgment tracking
acceptanceCriteria: Alerts are created automatically based on threshold violations
Alerts include severity classification (info, warning, critical)
Users can acknowledge and resolve alerts

requirements.text: Create a frontend dashboard displaying real-time campus operations overview with device status summary, active alerts count, current sensor readings, and system health metrics
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows aggregated statistics across all devices
Real-time updates reflect current system state
Visual indicators for system health and alert status

requirements.text: Build frontend device management interface with searchable/filterable list of all IoT devices, showing type, location, status, and last reading, with ability to view device details and history
acceptanceCriteria: Devices can be filtered by type, location, and status
Search functionality finds devices by ID or location
Device detail view shows complete information and reading history

requirements.text: Create frontend automation rules interface where users can create, edit, enable/disable rules with visual condition builder and action selector
acceptanceCriteria: Users can define rules without technical knowledge
Rule conditions support comparison operators and logical combinations
Actions can target specific devices or device groups

requirements.text: Build frontend analytics view displaying historical sensor data with interactive charts showing trends over time, energy consumption patterns, and occupancy analytics by building or zone
acceptanceCriteria: Charts visualize sensor data trends over selectable time ranges
Data can be filtered by device type, location, or metric
Export functionality for reports and analysis

requirements.text: Create frontend alerts and notifications panel showing active alerts sorted by severity, with filtering options and ability to acknowledge or resolve alerts
acceptanceCriteria: Alerts are displayed with clear severity indicators
Users can filter alerts by type, severity, or status
Alert actions (acknowledge, resolve) update backend state

requirements.text: Build frontend AI recommendations view displaying optimization suggestions with priority, estimated impact, implementation instructions, and accept/dismiss actions
acceptanceCriteria: Recommendations are presented with clear priority and impact metrics
Each recommendation includes actionable implementation steps
Users can accept (create automation rule) or dismiss recommendations

requirements.text: Implement role-based access control with at least three roles: Admin (full system access), Operator (device monitoring and rule management), and Viewer (read-only access to dashboards and analytics)
acceptanceCriteria: Users are assigned specific roles with defined permissions
Backend enforces role-based access for all operations
Unauthorized access attempts are rejected with appropriate errors

requirements.text: Create a visually cohesive design system with a modern tech-forward aesthetic using mint green and slate gray as primary colors, with clean geometric layouts and subtle data visualization accents that convey efficiency and intelligence
acceptanceCriteria: All UI components follow consistent color scheme and typography
Design conveys professionalism suitable for university operations
Visual hierarchy clearly distinguishes primary actions from secondary content

constraints: Backend must use single-actor Motoko architecture with all logic in main actor
Frontend must use React with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Shadcn components
Do not modify immutable frontend paths: hooks/useInternetIdentity, hooks/useActor, main.tsx, components/ui
Authentication must use Internet Identity only
No external databases, cloud providers, or third-party API integrations
No real-time WebSocket features or push notifications
nonGoals: Physical IoT device firmware or hardware integration
Actual machine learning model training or AI inference
Integration with existing university systems or databases
Video surveillance or physical security systems
